tests: Superscript footnote markers in body text and a footnote block below a partial-width rule.
attacks: Reading order and note association. The markers are tiny isolated digits sitting above the baseline — candidates for being dropped, merged into the adjacent word ('74.2%1'), or promoted as their own elements. The footnote block is small text after a rule and may be read as page furniture and artifacted away, which would delete the statement that the two bowel figures are not comparable.
title: Screening Coverage Note

footnotes.text: Weighted by eligible population at the mid-year estimate.
Bowel screening moved from a two-year to a 30-month cycle in the prior year; the two figures are not directly comparable.
Rounding applied at one decimal place throughout.

mustNotBeArtifacts: the footnote block — it carries substantive qualification, not page furniture
intentionalProblems: superscript markers may merge into adjacent text
